newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London and Frankfurt stocks hit peaks, pause.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London and Frankfurt stocks hit peaks, pause.

text.p: London and Frankfurt stocks roared ahead to new trading peaks on Tuesday then paused for breath as Wall Street made an unsettled opening on profit-taking.

On currency markets the dollar was weaker but sterling bounded forward after Britain raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point. The move, coupled with sweeping monetray reforms by the new Labour administration, also gave a big lift to government bonds.

Most of the action was in equity markets. London raced ahead by 1.5 percent to 4525.6 points on the FTSE index in morning trading , boosted by a blistering overnight rally in New York which drove Wall Street to a record close.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped slightly as Wall Street fell at the opening -- only to claw its way back into profit within the first hour of trading.

Frankfurt floor trade ended at a record close of 3,568.28 points, eclipsing the previous best set only yesterday. But after-hours computerised transactions were rattled by Wall Street's weak start and fell 0.4 percent.

Madrid and Brussels too were in bullish mood, reaching new peaks in the morning session. In strong contrast Paris fell and by late-afternoon was down by 0.8 percent, buffeted by political uncertainties.

The push for initial advances in Europe came from New York's performance on Monday where stocks were lifted by hopes that a balanced budget agreement would keep the U.S. central bank from raising interest rates later this month.

But the London market was given an extra shove by the new finance minister Gordon Brown who ended uncertainty by making a small interest rate increase and gave the central bank independence to set interest rate policy.
British shares had pruned back opening gains in a bout of jitters after the regular monthly monetary meeting between the government and the Bank of England was suddenly brought forward by one day.
But the FTSE bounced back after the interest rate announcement.
"Everyone was expecting a 25 basis point rise and that's what they got, the gilt market should certainly like this," said Steve Wright, BZW UK equity strategist.
"The (equity) futures had sold off ahead of this news on worries that the rate rise might be half a point and that would have been seen as overly aggressive," said one futures specialist.

Just days into the new government the leading FTSE index has responded with record performances, setting an intraday peak of 4,468.4 on Friday, the last trading day because of a public holiday yesterday.
Besides raising rates to 6.25 percent from six percent, the new Labour government gave the central bank greater powers in a radical move that changes the mechanics of setting monetary policy.

"Giving more independence to the Bank of England to set interest rates is probably more significant than the fact that interest rates have gone up," said Wright at BZW. "It is a long way towards an independent central bank, which is a very Euro-friendly policy."

In Frankfurt, though floor trade ended at a new peak, computerised transactions had a rough time, hit by a see-sawing dollar and an uncertain Wall Street , before settling into calmer territory in the afternoon.
Prices had held steady or higher through the day until an initial weak opening on Wall Street and plunge by the dollar sent prices falling in low volume afternoon to show losses of 0.5 percent.
"It might be time to consolidate. ..," said one dealer. "It was alarming to see the market take such a beating today of all days." he added.
Paris stood out, the only major European bourse to show substantial losses. French stocks opened higher but quickly fell and were 0.8 percent down by early afternoon.
French investors were clearly anxious over the outcome of the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election which polls suggest will be a tight race.

On currency markets, the dollar weakened against the mark after the Bundesbank's Ernst Welteke said he could not welcome further rise in the U.S. currency. The dollar also fell against the yen. Fears about an interest rate rise in Japan are growing and the yen gained against both the dollar and mark overnight while Japanese government bond yields pushed higher.
Sterling had earlier stolen the limelight, climbing almost two pfennigs and more than one cent after the interest rate rise announcement before falling back.

"The market is looking more at the BOE independence measures than the rate rise and the forex market at least is taking the view that this will mean a tighter overall monetary policy than previously seen," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston. STOCKS PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 62.9 points at 4,518.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 18.50 points at 2,654.34.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 39.50 points at 3,568.28.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7237 marks compared with 1.7286 marks late in Europe on Monday. It was at 125.42 yen, compared to 126.62 on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.45 an ounce,
compared to Friday's close in London of $340.05. Silver was $4.75.
